Subject: Hosted API: data geography, retention windows & purge process

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Skyward is evaluating Redwood for several patient-facing inference flows. Security has a short set of follow-ups for our legal/risk review around hosted API data handling. Please confirm the following for hosted deployments:

1) Data geography: when we select the US region, are customer requests, logs, and model inputs/outputs stored only within us-east-1/ us-west-2 (we want single-country residency where possible)?
2) Retention windows: what are default retention periods for (a) request/response payloads, (b) KV cache / short-term inference caches, (c) audit logs and traces, and (d) backups and snapshots?
3) Deletion request SLA: if we submit an account-level data erasure request (tenant wipe), what are the steps and typical completion timeline? Any manual steps required on our side?
4) Backups & failover: do backups replicate cross-region by default? If so, can replication be disabled for customers requiring strict residency?
5) Evidence & attestation: can you provide SOC2 attestation and a short artifact showing retention/erasure controls for hosted API?

Our privacy team would like short answers we can include in the vendor review matrix. If you have a one-page matrix or slide, that helps.

Best,
Aisha
Security Program Manager
Skyward Health

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Answers below are oriented to Redwood Hosted API (not Dedicated/Private). I'll attach a one-page retention matrix and our latest SOC2 attestation for your review. If you want an architecture call with our security team I can schedule Soojin.

1) Data geography
- Customer requests (request metadata and full payloads when retained for analytics/quality) and standard logs are persisted in the cloud region you select (we currently support US, EU, APAC regions mapped to specific cloud zones). For US-hosted accounts we persist in the chosen us region (e.g., us-east-1). For customers requiring strict single-country residency we offer region isolation and can add contractual region-lock controls.

2) Retention windows (defaults; configurable per-account)
- Request/response payloads: default 30 days. Can be reduced to 0 (no retention) at provision time; note that disabling retention removes request-level analytics and certain quality monitoring features.
- Inference KV cache / ephemeral caches: typical TTL is 1 hour; caches are not written to persistent snapshots by default and are ephemeral to the serving runtime.
- Audit logs & traces: retained 90 days by default; can be extended for enterprise plans. Logs include routing decisions, model version, request id and latency metrics.
- Backups/snapshots: automated backups of platform metadata/indices retained 30 days; model artifacts follow the model catalog retention and are not customer payloads.

3) Tenant-level deletion (erasures)
- Process: submit a deletion request via the Console or your account rep (we also accept signed requests via DocuSign). We produce a deletion plan, schedule a wipe job, and run verification passes.
- Timeline: typical SLA is 30 calendar days end-to-end for hosted accounts. Urgent erasures (regulatory requests) can be expedited to 5 business days with an approved support escalation and audit trail.
- Customer actions: none required for standard erasure; to fully invalidate cached results you may request a TTL purge which we coordinate. If you have exported backups, please provide confirmation if you want those revoked (we can coordinate with S3 lifecycle policies).

4) Backups & replication
- By default, platform control-plane metadata backups are stored in the same region and may replicate for resilience within cloud-region constructs. Cross-region backups are not enabled for US single-region customers unless explicitly turned on as part of DR requirements. We can disable automatic cross-region replication for accounts with strict residency needs.

5) Evidence & attestation
- Attached: "retention_matrix_v1.xlsx" (one-page matrix) and our current "SOC2_Attestation.pdf". For deeper evidence we can furnish architecture diagrams and ephemeral logs on a scoped basis under NDA.

Notes & caveats
- De-identification & aggregation: we can offer request-level redaction pipelines to strip PHI before retention; this typically requires configuration at onboarding.
- Billing/metrics: usage events (token counts) are retained for billing reconciliation for 365 days by default; aggregated billing reports persist longer as needed for financial audit.

Next steps: I'll loop Soojin to confirm the expedited erasure path and propose a short call if you want the security team to walk through the retention matrix.

Best,

Hi Aisha — quick follow-up from security operations with a few clarifications:

- Verification: after a tenant wipe we run three verification passes: record delete, KV cache invalidate, and log sync check. We log an audit record for each pass and provide a signed attestation of completion on request.
- Emergency legal holds: if Skyward needs a temporary legal hold we can pause scheduled erasures; this is a manual operation initiated by your security contact with an approved ticket.
- Encryption: all customer payloads at rest are encrypted KMS-managed. If you bring your own key (BYOK) we can integrate via your KMS for hosted accounts in supported clouds; BYOK does not change retention settings but allows you to rotate/revoke key access.

If you'd like, we can run a short tabletop demonstrating an erasure request and show the audit logs (redacted) we produce.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
